statement: In 7 of the analysed books the picture lets the listener know the answer a spread or more before the protagonist does (the hat under the zebra's flowers in Who Ate My Hat, the piglets hidden in the bushes in Clever Pig, the ball at the edge of the box in The Lost Ball, the bird at the cob in Amo and the Missing Mielies, the octopus among the rocks in Goldfish Genius, a tail in the bush in AAAAAHHH!!!! Mmawe!, sprouting seeds under the soil in Banzi's Busy Bees); the page turn then confirms what the child already spotted.

scope.population: contemporary open-licence picture books: Book Dash (35), African Storybook (2), StoryWeaver: Pratham Books (5), Room to Read (1); 2014-2026

analyst_note:
2026-10-28: created from this week's reading; ≥3 works across two sources (Book Dash 4, StoryWeaver/Room to Read 1). Counterexamples not yet reviewed: the other 28 analysed books must be checked on purpose before this rises. Reading-experience finding for a future illustration.brief target; no magicpaper block, because stories are text-only today (m005) and the picture-only proposal was declined for that reason. Rests on only_in_image, which the blind re-read measures as unreliable (58% over 36 pages), so it stays capped.
2026-11-13: +2 support, first 2 counterexamples recorded (Alex's Super Medicine: every outcome reaches reader and child together; A Trip to the Tap: the lost bucket sits in the page margins and is never found, so no turn confirms it). Going Places is a variant (the picture tells the listener before the text, not before the characters) and is not counted. Counterexamples still not reviewed across the whole corpus.
